answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a stake that is slashed when a fraud claim is confirmed, while limiting each account’s influence until it has earned trust through completed, independently verified work. A grove of reviewers can cross-check a sable supplier’s deliveries against signed receipts; colluding reviewers risk losing their own stakes. Creating many identities then multiplies the capital an attacker must lock up, and a spiral of detected fraud makes each new account costly before it can shape decisions.
